mainTopic: Does the ban on an egg laid on ראש השנה still stand after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה? The amud draws on the rule that a decree made by vote needs a new vote to cancel it.
overview: The amud finishes the ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's כרם רבעי. His students tell him that his colleagues, led by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, already voted to cancel the decree. From this the גמרא learns that a decree made by a vote needs a new vote to end it, even when its reason is gone. Two verses from מתן תורה prove the same rule, and the case of כרם רבעי shows that it applies to bans that are דרבנן too. רב יוסף uses this rule to keep the egg of ראש השנה forbidden, because רבן יוחנן בן זכאי voted only about witnesses, not about the egg. אביי answers that the egg was never voted on separately: it depended on the witness rule, so it became permitted along with it. רב אדא and רב שלמן still forbid the egg, out of fear of a mix-up once the בית המקדש is rebuilt, and רבא forbids it because even today the two days can be one holiness. רבא ends by ruling that the הלכה follows רב in his three rulings, whether lenient or strict.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר wants to make his vineyard ownerless, and his students stop him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי אליעזר wanted to make his fourth-year fruit הפקר for the poor. His students told him the חכמים had already voted to permit redeeming it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he wanted to declare it ownerless for the poor. His students said to him: רבי, your colleagues already took a vote about you and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's כרם רבעי. It is quoted as a proof for רב יוסף's rule about votes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was a decree that כרם רבעי fruit grown within a day's travel of ירושלים had to be brought there to decorate its markets, not redeemed. רבי אליעזר's vineyard was close by, so he could not redeem the fruit, and he thought of giving it away to the poor instead. His students told him the decree had already been cancelled by a formal vote.

keyTerms.meaning: to make it ownerless (הפקר), free for anyone to take
they took a count / formal vote
and they permitted it
a vineyard's fourth-year fruit, which must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed

steps.confusionAlert: This story is not mainly about vineyard laws. It is brought only to show how a decree gets cancelled: by a new vote.

phrases.english: And he sought to make it ownerless for the poor.
phrases.notes: Poor people would find it worthwhile to carry the fruit to ירושלים.

phrases.english: His students said to him: Rabbi,
your colleagues already voted regarding you and permitted it.
phrases.notes: The decree requiring the fruit to be brought to ירושלים had been formally cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous section of the דף.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's rule that a decree made by vote needs another vote to cancel it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about רבי אליעזר's כרם רבעי near לוד.

steps.title: Who were the 'colleagues'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who 'your colleagues' were and answers: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are 'your colleagues'? רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to identify who took the vote that cancelled the decree. It is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and his court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us the decree was cancelled by a recognized בית דין, after the חורבן. The decorating reason no longer applied once the בית המקדש was destroyed. Even so, a real vote was taken.

keyTerms.meaning: who?
leader of the חכמים in יבנה after the חורבן

phrases.english: Who are 'your colleagues'?
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a phrase in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'colleagues' who voted.

steps.title: The inference: without a vote, the decree would still stand
steps.stepSummary: The decree was permitted only because they voted. Without a vote, it would not have been permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that they voted. But if they had not voted, it would not be permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls the actual proof out of the story. The fruit became permitted only because of the vote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the decree, decorating ירושלים, was already gone after the חורבן. If that alone ended the decree, no vote would have been needed. So a decree made by vote stays until another vote cancels it, which supports רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is that... (introduces an inference)
but if not...

steps.whatToRemember: A decree does not expire on its own when its reason disappears. A new vote is needed to cancel it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core idea behind רב יוסף's ruling. An enactment stays in force, even when its original reason seems to be gone, until it is formally cancelled.

phrases.english: The reason is that they voted.
But had they not voted — no (it would not be permitted).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal inference from the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: כל דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אליעזר's vineyard: permission came only through a vote.

steps.title: Why did רב יוסף bring a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יוסף meant by 'and it says', which added another verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move. It asks why רב יוסף needed a second verse when he brought his proof from מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב יוסף quoted 'היו נכונים לשלשת ימים' and then said 'ואומר', adding 'לך אמור להם שובו לכם לאהליכם'. Adding a second verse with 'ואומר' suggests the first was not enough. The גמרא wants to know what the second verse adds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and it says', which introduces an additional verse
what?

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'and it says'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the ברייתא proof to explaining רב יוסף's verse proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יוסף needed the second verse.

steps.title: The second verse is the real proof: 'Return to your tents' would be unnecessary otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition at סיני was only for three days. So 'go back to your tents' would be unneeded unless a new permission was required, and that shows a vote-based prohibition needs a new permission to end.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means. Since it is written 'Be ready for three days, do not come near a woman', why do I need 'Go tell them: return to your tents'? Learn from this: anything set by a count needs another count to permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second verse is where the proof actually comes from. The first verse only sets up the time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on being with their wives had a built-in end, three days. One would think it simply expired by itself. But the תורה still says 'return to your tents', which teaches that even a time-limited prohibition set by a count needs an explicit permission to end.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he is saying
since / now, seeing that
why do I need it?
learn from this
a count / formal vote

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the first verse is the proof. It only shows the ban already had an end date. The proof is that the תורה still needed to say 'return'.
steps.whatToRemember: כל דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו: anything set by a vote or count needs a new vote or count to permit it.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying: since it is written,
'Be ready for the third day,'
'do not come near a woman,'
then 'Go say to them,'
'Return to your tents' — why do I need it?
phrases.notes: After three days the ban would end anyway.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that anything established by a count
requires another count to permit it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second verse would be unneeded if the time-limited ban simply ended. So it proves that a new permission is required.
steps.raayaObject: כל דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'שובו לכם לאהליכם' after the three-day ban at סיני.

steps.title: Maybe 'Return to your tents' was about the marital obligation
steps.stepSummary: A possible objection: perhaps 'return to your tents' was a command to fulfill מצות עונה, not a permission ending the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: it came for the מצוה of conjugal duty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible way to knock down the proof from 'return to your tents'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse was a positive command to go home and fulfill מצות עונה, it was not needed to permit anything. Then it proves nothing about needing a new vote, so the proof is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
a husband's obligation of regular marital relations
that it came (for)

phrases.english: And if you say:
it came for the מצוה of conjugal duty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof drawn in the previous step.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse has a different purpose, a command for מצות עונה. So it is not extra and teaches nothing about cancelling a ban.

steps.title: A new proof: 'When the שופר sounds long, they may go up the mountain'
steps.stepSummary: To answer the objection, the גמרא brings another verse from סיני: 'במשך היובל המה יעלו בהר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'When the ram's horn sounds long, they may go up the mountain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a new proof from a different verse. The next step explains how this verse proves the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mountain was forbidden to the people during מתן תורה, and this verse says they may go up when the shofar sounds long. That suggests the ban needed an explicit signal of permission to end. It strengthens רב יוסף's rule without relying on the verse that was questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a proof)
when the ram's horn is drawn out (sounds long)
they may go up the mountain

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'When the ram's horn sounds long, they may go up the mountain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection by bringing a different verse as proof.
steps.raayaObject: כל דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו
steps.raayaSupportSource: 'במשך היובל המה יעלו בהר': the mountain became permitted only through an explicit signal.

steps.title: Why the extra signal at סיני proves the rule
steps.stepSummary: Since the animals were only barred while the שכינה was on the mountain, the extra signal of the שופר must have been a new permission. This proves that a דבר שבמנין needs another vote to permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה already says the flocks and herds may not graze near the mountain. So why do we need the verse 'when the ram's horn sounds long'? Learn from this: something forbidden by a vote needs another vote to permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the verse brought in the last step proves רב יוסף's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse already shows that the ban on the mountain was temporary. A special signal to end it would be unnecessary unless ending a formal ban needs a formal act of permission. That signal is the 'new vote' that permits what the first vote forbade.

keyTerms.meaning: Now since (introduces a logical setup)
Why do I need it? (the verse seems extra)
Learn from this
A matter decided by a vote of the court
Another vote

steps.whatToRemember: דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו: a ban made by a vote stays in force until another vote cancels it, even if the reason for the ban is gone.

phrases.english: Now since it is written:
"Neither shall the flocks nor the herds graze
in front of that mountain",
why do I need "when the ram's horn sounds long"?
phrases.notes: The first verse already shows that the ban was only temporary.

phrases.english: Learn from this:
a matter established by a vote
requires another vote to permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof introduced in step 7 and answers the objection from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: דבר שבמנין צריך מנין אחר להתירו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra verse at סיני, 'במשך היובל המה יעלו בהר', compared with 'גם הצאן והבקר אל ירעו'.

steps.title: Maybe the rule only applies to דאורייתא, not דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: One could argue that the need for a new vote only applies to bans that are דאורייתא, like the one at סיני, not to bans that are דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: this applies only to דאורייתא, but not to דרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible limit on the rule it just proved. This sets up the next step, which will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof came from סיני, which was a situation of דאורייתא. Perhaps decrees that are דרבנן, like the egg ban, are weaker and end on their own once their reason is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (an anticipated objection)
These words apply (only)
Torah law
Rabbinic law

phrases.english: And if you will say
this applies only to Torah law,
but to rabbinic law, it does not

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to limit the rule proven in step 8 to Torah law.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the rule of step 8 to rabbinic decrees such as the egg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is a Torah situation, so it may not extend to rabbinic bans.

steps.title: כרם רבעי shows the rule applies to bans that are דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: The rule requiring fruit of כרם רבעי to be brought to ירושלים was דרבנן. Even so, it needed a vote of the colleagues to cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear the case of כרם רבעי. The rule of כרם רבעי is דרבנן, and still they told רבי אליעזר: your colleagues already voted and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection by proving that even a rabbinic ban needed a new vote to end it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rabbinic bans ended on their own, nobody would have needed to say 'your colleagues voted.' The fact that a vote was mentioned shows that a rabbinic decree also needs a new vote to be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introducing a proof)
Fruit of a vineyard in its fourth year
They voted
Your colleagues

phrases.english: Come and hear: the fourth-year vineyard,
and the rule of the fourth-year vineyard is rabbinic,
phrases.notes: The rule to bring it to ירושלים instead of redeeming it was a תקנה דרבנן.

phrases.english: and they said to him (רבי אליעזר):
your colleagues have already voted on it for you and permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit proposed in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: A rabbinic דבר שבמנין also needs another vote to permit it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רבי אליעזר and כרם רבעי.

steps.title: Didn't רבן יוחנן בן זכאי already vote to permit the egg?
steps.stepSummary: One might say the second vote already happened, because רבן יוחנן בן זכאי voted and permitted the egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: the egg also had a vote. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי and his court voted on it and permitted it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: even under the rule, maybe a new vote for the egg already took place. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף holds that the egg is still forbidden. But if רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה counts as the 'new vote,' the egg should be permitted again.

keyTerms.meaning: The egg laid on ראש השנה
They voted
They permitted it
The leading sage after the destruction of the Temple

phrases.english: And if you will say:
the egg too,

phrases.aramaic: אִמְּנוֹ עֲלַהּ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי voted on it
and they permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the rule but asks whether its condition (a new vote) was already met for the egg.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the egg is still forbidden today.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second vote by רבן יוחנן בן זכאי already took place, so the ban should be over.

steps.title: The vote was about witnesses, not the egg
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's vote only restored accepting witnesses all day. It never addressed the egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they voted, it was about the testimony. About the egg, they did not vote.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the later vote was on a different topic, so the egg ban still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי allowed witnesses of the new moon to be accepted all day again. Since the egg was not part of that vote, according to רב יוסף the egg still has no 'new vote' to permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony of witnesses who saw the new moon
Regarding, about

phrases.english: When they voted, it was about the testimony;
about the egg, they did not vote.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the later vote
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's vote counted as permitting the egg.
steps.terutzMaskana: His vote covered only the witnesses, so the egg ban remains in force according to רב יוסף.

steps.title: אביי: the egg was never banned by its own vote
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's whole approach. The egg was never a separate vote. Its ban depended entirely on the rule about witnesses, so once that rule changed, the egg became permitted automatically.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Was the egg ever banned by a vote? The egg depends on the testimony. When testimony was forbidden, the egg was forbidden. When testimony was permitted, the egg was permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב יוסף's claim at its root: the rule of דבר שבמנין does not apply to the egg at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed the egg was its own decree that needed its own new vote. אביי says the egg was only a side effect of the ban on late witnesses. When the cause was cancelled, its result fell away with it, so no separate vote was ever needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (introduces a rhetorical rejection)
The matter depends on
Became forbidden
Became permitted

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the egg ban was never its own decree. It depended on the witness rule, so when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי restored the witness rule, the egg became permitted automatically.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not reject the rule of דבר שבמנין itself. He only rejects applying it to the egg, because the egg was never voted on separately.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key distinction: a ban that was formally voted on needs a new vote to end it, but a result that only follows from another rule ends when that rule ends.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (Rav Yosef):
Is that to say the egg was forbidden by a vote?
The egg's status depends on the testimony.
When testimony was forbidden, the egg was forbidden;
when testimony was permitted, the egg was permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי אַטּוּ בֵּיצָה בְּמִנְיָן מִי הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind steps 8 to 12 that the egg was a דבר שבמנין.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב יוסף's application of דבר שבמנין to the egg (not the rule itself).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The egg was never voted on separately. Its ban was only a result of the witness rule, so it ended automatically when that rule was restored.

steps.title: רב אדא and רב שלמן: The egg stays forbidden because of a future mix-up
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא and רב שלמן rule that even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה, the egg is still forbidden. They fear confusion once the בית המקדש is rebuilt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא and רב שלמן, both from בי כלוחית, said: Even from the time of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ordinance onward, an egg is still forbidden. Why? The בית המקדש may soon be rebuilt. Then people will say: 'Last year, didn't we eat an egg on the second day of יום טוב? So now we can eat it too.' They won't realize that last year the two days were two separate holinesses, while now they are one holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree with אביי's conclusion and say the egg is still forbidden today. Their reason is to prevent a mistake in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Today the two days of ראש השנה are two separate holinesses, so an egg from day one could have been allowed on day two. But when the בית המקדש is rebuilt, the old rule (witnesses accepted only until מנחה) will return, and both days will become one long holiness, where the egg is truly forbidden. People used to eating it would keep eating it by mistake, so we forbid it already now.

keyTerms.meaning: From בי כלוחית, a place name
The בית המקדש will soon be rebuilt
Last year (the past practice people remember)
Two separate holinesses: each day stands on its own
One holiness: both days count as one long holy day

steps.confusionAlert: 'אשתקד' (last year) here means our current situation, as seen from the future after the בית המקדש is rebuilt. 'השתא' (now) means that future time. It is easy to read these backwards.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the egg can stay forbidden even though its original reason (witnesses only until מנחה) is gone. It is a protective rule for the future.

phrases.english: Rav Adda and Rav Shalman,
both of them from Bei Keloḥit, said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ
phrases.english: Even from the ordinance of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai onward
an egg is forbidden.
What is the reason?
The Temple will soon be rebuilt,
phrases.notes: Then the old rule of accepting witnesses only until מנחה will return.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֹאמְרוּ: אֶשְׁתָּקַד מִי לֹא אָכַלְנוּ בֵּיצָה
phrases.english: and people will say: Last year, didn't we eat an egg
on the second day of the Festival?
Now too we will eat it.
But they will not know
that last year they were two separate holinesses,
and now it is one holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא וְרַב שַׁלְמָן תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִבֵּי כְלוֹחִית אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's conclusion in Step 13 that the egg became permitted automatically.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The egg remains forbidden even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה, so people won't make a mistake when the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

steps.title: Then we should not accept witnesses all day either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the same worry should stop us from accepting witnesses all day today, yet we do accept them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should also not accept testimony all day. Why? The בית המקדש will soon be rebuilt, and people will say: 'Last year, didn't we accept testimony about the new month all day? Now too we will accept it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אדא and רב שלמן's reasoning by applying it to the witnesses themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we fear people will carry today's habits into the future, then accepting witnesses all day should also be forbidden. Once the בית המקדש is rebuilt, witnesses will only be accepted until מנחה. But רבן יוחנן בן זכאי clearly allowed witnesses all day, so this kind of future worry should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge that follows from the previous logic
Testimony about seeing the new moon
The entire day

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, עֵדוּת נָמֵי לֹא נְקַבֵּל,
phrases.english: If so, we should also not accept testimony,
What is the reason?
The Temple will soon be rebuilt,
and people will say: Last year, didn't we accept
testimony about the new month the entire day?
Now too we will accept it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי עֵדוּת נָמֵי לֹא נְקַבֵּל
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא and רב שלמן's concern about future confusion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same future-confusion worry would forbid accepting witnesses all day, which רבן יוחנן בן זכאי clearly allowed.

steps.title: Witnesses are handled by the court, but eggs are handled by everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. The בית דין handles witnesses and won't get confused. Eggs are in everyone's hands, so ordinary people may get confused.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, testimony is handed over to the בית דין. An egg is handed over to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אדא and רב שלמן by showing why the worry applies to eggs but not to witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the בית דין decides whether to accept witnesses, and they know the rules. They will not mistakenly copy the old practice. Eggs are eaten by ordinary people at home, who might not ask a חכם, so a mix-up is a real risk.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? Rejects a comparison
Handed over to the court (only experts handle it)
Handed over to everyone (ordinary people handle it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common principle: חכמים worry more about mistakes in things ordinary people do on their own than in things only a בית דין handles.

phrases.english: How can you compare!
There, testimony is entrusted to the court.
An egg is entrusted to everyone.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (who handles the matter)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The future-confusion worry should apply equally to witnesses and to eggs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry applies only to eggs, which everyone handles, and not to witnesses, which the expert בית דין handles.

steps.title: רבא also rules the egg stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא agrees that the egg is still forbidden even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה. In the next step he gives a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even from the time of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ordinance onward, an egg is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states the same ruling as רב אדא and רב שלמן. This sets up his own, different reason, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is the same as in Step 14, but רבא is a new speaker with a new reason. He does not rely on a fear of future confusion. Instead, he will argue the egg is truly forbidden even today.

keyTerms.meaning: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ordinance to accept witnesses all day
And onward

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ
phrases.english: Even from the ordinance of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai onward
an egg is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אַף מִתַּקָּנַת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי וְאֵילָךְ בֵּיצָה אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaches the same ruling as Step 14, setting up a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The egg remains forbidden even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה.

steps.title: Even רבן יוחנן בן זכאי keeps both days holy when witnesses come late
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his point: even רבן יוחנן בן זכאי agrees that if witnesses come after מנחה, both that day and the next day are kept holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבן יוחנן בן זכאי agree that if witnesses came from מנחה time and later, we keep that day as holy and the next day as holy too?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his ruling with a fact that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even under רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's system, there are cases where both days are kept holy together. That shows the two days of ראש השנה in ארץ ישראל can be one long holiness even today. So an egg laid on day one is truly forbidden on day two, not just because of a future worry.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't he agree? A rhetorical question used as proof
From the afternoon (מנחה) time and later
We keep / we practice

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons the egg stays forbidden after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. רב אדא and רב שלמן say it is to prevent a future mistake, since eggs are in everyone's hands. רבא says that even today both days can be one holiness, so the egg is truly forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: מִי לֹא מוֹדֶה רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: Doesn't Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai agree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם בָּאוּ עֵדִים מִן הַמִּנְחָה וּלְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: that if witnesses came from minḥa time and later,
we observe that day as holy
and the next day as holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לֹא מוֹדֶה רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason and proof for רבא's ruling in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the egg stays forbidden even after רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's own agreement that when witnesses come after מנחה, both days are kept holy

steps.title: The הלכה follows רב in all three rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that the הלכה follows רב in three of his rulings about two-day ימים טובים, whether the ruling is lenient or strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The הלכה follows רב in these three rulings, both where he is lenient and where he is strict.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the discussion with a practical ruling: in these three cases we follow רב, whether his ruling is lenient or strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רב gave three rulings about two-day ימים טובים. Two are lenient: an egg laid on the first day of the two יום טוב days outside ארץ ישראל is allowed on the second day, and a person may make a different עירוב for each day. One is strict: on ראש השנה the two days count as one holiness, so the egg stays forbidden. רבא tells us to follow רב in all three, even though they lead in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical halacha follows his opinion
In these three (rulings)
In the lenient direction
In the strict direction

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: follow רב. Outside ארץ ישראל, the two days of יום טוב are treated as two separate holinesses, so the rulings are lenient. On ראש השנה, the two days are treated as one long holiness, so the egg stays forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is contradicting himself by being both lenient and strict. The three rulings rest on one idea. Regular two-day יום טוב outside ארץ ישראל is two separate days, which leads to leniency. ראש השנה is one long day, which leads to strictness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line for the whole discussion of an egg laid on יום טוב, and it is the basis for how these הלכות are actually followed.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
phrases.notes: Same רבא who just argued that the egg is forbidden on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: The halacha is in accordance with Rav
phrases.notes: This is a practical ruling, not just a theory.

phrases.english: in these three [rulings],
phrases.notes: The three rulings of רב discussed earlier in the סוגיא: the egg on the two days of יום טוב outside ארץ ישראל, the two עירובין, and the egg on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: whether to be lenient or to be strict.
phrases.notes: Two of the rulings are lenient and one is strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא proved that the egg is forbidden on ראש השנה (Step 18), he now gives the overall practical ruling, adopting all three of רב's rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רב in his three rulings about two-day ימים טובים, both the lenient and the strict ones.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Follow רב. Outside ארץ ישראל, the two days of יום טוב are separate, so the egg is allowed on the second day and two separate עירובין may be made. On ראש השנה, the two days are one holiness, so the egg remains forbidden.
